findings.title: Date-override slots skip busy checks and can be double-booked
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, once dateOverrideExist is set and the function has not returned false, it returns true immediately at lines 133-135. This happens before the busy array is checked at line 153. Slots are generated by getTimeSlots without considering busy, so a fixed or loose host with a date override is treated as available even when they have an accepted booking or calendar event during that override. Date overrides should replace normal working hours, not suppress busy checks.

findings.title: Working-hours validation uses slot start for both start and end
findings.body: The new working-hours check computes `const start = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` and then `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`, so it never tests slotEndTime. A slot that starts inside the host's work hours but ends after `workingHour.endTime` is not rejected. For round-robin fixed hosts, getTimeSlots can produce such slots from other hosts' longer availability, so fixed hosts can be booked outside their actual working hours.

findings.title: Multiple date overrides on the same day are not all evaluated
findings.body: The date-override validation uses `dateOverrides.find` and returns true as soon as the slot is outside one same-day override, which makes checkIfIsAvailable return false immediately. If a host has multiple same-day date overrides (for example 09:00-10:00 and 14:00-15:00), a slot in the second override is rejected because the first override does not contain it. Only if no same-day override contains the slot should the slot be considered outside the overridden availability.

findings.title: Split working-hours windows are not all evaluated
findings.body: The normal working-hours validation similarly uses `workingHours.find` and returns true when a single same-day working-hour window does not contain the slot. A host with split hours (for example 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-17:00) will be treated as unavailable for slots in the later window because the first window is checked first and the function returns false before checking the second. The check should pass if any working-hours window contains the slot, not fail if the first one does not.

findings.title: Date override day filter still uses unadjusted organizer wall time
findings.body: activeOverrides filters overrides by comparing `dayjs.utc(override.start)` with the invitee day. `override.start` is the organizer-local wall time encoded as a UTC timestamp (for example 14:00 IST is stored as T14:00Z), not the actual UTC instant. The new offset conversion later in the function fixes slot minutes but this filter is still applied before that conversion. For attendee timezones whose UTC day differs from the organizer's encoded day, the override can be applied to the previous or next day, so the correct day shows wrong availability.

findings.title: No test covers fixed-host date overrides in round-robin events
findings.body: The new test only exercises a personal event and checks that the returned UTC slots remain the same for a different attendee timezone. The main round-robin fixed-host date-override behavior is untested. A round-robin event with fixed and loose hosts, where the fixed host has a date override, should be added to verify the fix and would have exposed the busy-time and working-hours issues in checkIfIsAvailable.
